Impudent

/IM-pyuh-duhnt/ - the stress falls on IM · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Impudent means boldly rude and disrespectful; shamelessly cheeky.

No one expected the intern to grade the director's own slides and hand them back marked 'B-minus' — an impudent stunt that somehow earned a laugh.

Worked Example

When the quiz-show host mispronounced 'quinoa,' the contestant corrected her on air — then did it again in the lightning round, grinning wider each time.

Impudent goes past cheeky: the cheeky remark keeps a wink of affection, but the impudent one is shameless — im- ('not') + pudere ('to feel shame'), disrespect with the blush removed. Its cousin impertinent (this unit) stresses the overstep; impudent stresses the missing shame.

How Impudent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

cheeky

cheeky: playfully bold — the mild, affectionate end of this family

brash

brash: loudly overconfident, pushy rather than disrespectful

Antonyms

respectful

respectful: minding rank and feeling — shame intact

meek

meek: so mild it wouldn't dream of talking back

How Strong Is It? — cheeky → saucy → impudent

cheeky vs. impudent

cheeky vs. impudent: Cheeky is playful boldness that still means well — it stops far short of impudent, which has stopped caring how it lands.

saucy vs. impudent

saucy vs. impudent: Saucy talk is bolder than cheeky but still winks at its own naughtiness; it stops short of impudent, which drops the shame altogether.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — im-

Prefix — im-: not (in- before p)

Root — -pud-

Root — -pud-: to feel shame (Latin pudere)

Suffix — -ent

Suffix — -ent: adjective: in a state of

Put it together

Put it together: A true 'not' word: im- ('not,' before p) + pudere ('to feel shame') + -ent. The impudent speaker is literally un-ashamed — the blush deleted. English kept almost nothing else from pudere, which is why this family tree is so short.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: Impudent is im- ('not') + Latin pudere, 'to feel shame' — shame-less, exactly as it behaves. But pudere left almost nothing else behind in everyday English: beyond impudent and its noun impudence, the family died out, so there is no common cousin to practice the root on.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Impudent is the word for disrespect delivered without a flicker of shame — bolder than cheeky, and blunter than impertinent, which marks the polite line being crossed (both are in this unit). Saucy and sassy are its playground cousins; impudent belongs in the headmaster's report.
